title.fr: Échographie : endophtalmie et abcès orbitaire

caption.fr: A : collection hypoéchogène (astérisque) dans la partie latérale de l’orbite = abcès orbitaire. B : débris purulents échogènes, irréguliers et cloisonnés dans le vitré (étoile) = signe clé de l’endophtalmie. C, D : zone hypoéchogène en arrière de la rétine et de la choroïde (pointes de flèche) = liquide dans l’espace sous-ténonien ; fine membrane croisant le nerf optique (flèches) = décollement postérieur du vitré.
caption.en: A: hypoechoic fluid collection (asterisk) in the lateral orbit = orbital abscess. B: echogenic, irregular, loculated purulent debris in the vitreous (star) = key finding of endophthalmitis. C, D: hypoechoic region behind the retina and choroid (arrowheads) = fluid in sub-Tenon’s space; thin membrane crossing the optic nerve (arrows) = posterior vitreous detachment.

author: Haight et al. — Clin Pract Cases Emerg Med 2023;7(4)
article: Diagnosis of Endophthalmitis and Orbital Abscess by Ultrasound: A Case Report
source_description: (A) The hypoechoic fluid collection (asterisk) in the lateral aspect of the orbit is consistent with orbital abscess. (B) The echogenic purulent debris within the vitreous humor (star) has an irregular and loculated appearance and is the key ultrasonographic finding of endophthalmitis. (C) and (D) The hypoechoic region posterior to retina and choroid (arrowheads) represents fluid in sub-Tenon’s space (potential space), and the thin membrane crossing the optic nerve (arrows) represents a posterior vitreous detachment, both of which are less common ultrasonographic findings of endophthalmitis.

title.fr: OCT : traction vitréomaculaire → trou maculaire transfixiant → fermeture
title.en: OCT: vitreomacular traction → full-thickness macular hole → closure

caption.fr: SD-OCT avant et après vitrectomie. a : traction vitréomaculaire avec trou lamellaire externe et contour fovéolaire anormal (AV 0,04). b : J7 après vitrectomie avec pelage de la limitante interne : trou maculaire transfixiant avec espaces cystoïdes sur les deux berges (AV 0,08). c : 1 mois, trou fermé avec soulèvement de la couche des photorécepteurs et de la limitante externe dans la fovéa, microkystes intrarétiniens (AV 0,2). d : 5 mois, contour fovéolaire normal sans liquide (AV 0,5).
caption.en: SD-OCT before and after vitrectomy. a: vitreomacular traction with an outer lamellar macular hole and abnormal foveal contour (VA 0.04). b: day 7 after vitrectomy with ILM peeling: full-thickness macular hole with intraretinal cystoid spaces on both edges (VA 0.08). c: 1 month, closed hole with elevation of the photoreceptor layer and external limiting membrane in the fovea and intraretinal microcystoid spaces (VA 0.2). d: 5 months, normal foveal contour without subretinal fluid (VA 0.5).

author: Dominik Odrobina, Iwona Laudańska-Olszewska, Piotr Gozdek et al. — BMC Ophthalmology 2014
article: Macular hole formation and spontaneous closure after vitrectomy for vitreomacular traction documented in spectral-domain optical coherence tomography
source_description: Spectral-optical coherence tomography before and after vitrectomy for vitreomacular traction. a: A 78-year-old female presented with visual acuity 0.04 and metamorphopsia. SD-OCT examination showed the vitreomacular traction (VMT) with an outer lamellar macular hole and an abnormal foveal contour. b: Seven days after the vitrectomy with ILM peeling visual acuity increased to 0.08. SD-OCT showed the full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) with intraretinal cystoid spaces on the both edges of the hole. c: One month later the patient presented with increased of visual acuity to 0.2. SD-OCT clearly documented closed macular hole with an elevation of the photoreceptor layer and of the external limiting membrane (ELM) in the fovea region and intraretinal microcystoid spaces. d: 5 months later visual acuity improved to 0.5. SD-OCT examination showed normal fovea contour without subretinal fluid with no evidence of space in the outer layers of the retina.
